decision_conditions:
The works proposed relate to branches encroaching from a tree located on neighbouring land. Under common law, a landowner has the right to cut back branches or roots that overhang or encroach onto their property, but only as far as the boundary line. This right does not require the consent of the tree owner, provided access to the neighbouring land is not required and no greater works are undertaken than are necessary to remove the encroachment.

Any material arising from such works remains the property of the tree owner and should be offered back unless otherwise agreed. Care should be taken to ensure that works do not extend beyond the applicant's legal rights, cause unnecessary damage to the tree, or result in trespass onto neighbouring land.

The granting of consent under the Tree Preservation Order legislation does not convey ownership rights, permission to enter adjacent land, or authority to undertake works beyond those permitted under common law. It remains the responsibility of the applicant to obtain any necessary permissions from the tree owner and to ensure that all works are undertaken lawfully.
description: Silk tree - Remove branches that overhang into property 15
